title: A PMCF-study on bioresorbable mm.PIP implant for the correction of lesser toe deformities
summary:
The PIP implant is used for bone reconstruction via joint stiffening (arthrodesis) of the lesser toes. This therapy, known as PIP arthrodesis, is used to surgically correct deformities of the small toes such as hammer or claw toes.
Suitable implants can be made of various materials providing different advantages and disadvantages. In recent decades, materials have been developed that are biodegradable and thus neither remain permanently in the body nor need to be removed again. 
One of such implants is the mm.PIP. The product is CE certified and available for clinical use. In this observational study, clinical data will be collected over a period of 12 months after insertion of the mm.PIP implant for the correction of hammer or claw toes during regular practice. In addition, data on patient satisfaction and pain of the study participants will be collected, the success of the surgery evaluated, and a functional score is taken.

interventions.name: • Pre-surgery: Physical examination (height, weight and organ systems); demographics; medical history; patient satisfaction assessed using a Likert scale; pain assessed using the VAS score and a Likert scale; American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS-LMIS) score; photo documentation; • Surger

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patient is able to give and provided informed consent for study participation
• Patient requires surgical correction of hammer or claw toes either isolated or in conjunction with distal Hallux valgus surgery
• Ability and willingness to adhere to study follow-up
Exclusion criteria:
• Contraindications for mm.PIP as indicated in the instructions for use
• Patient of a vulnerable group:
Patients with incurable diseases;
Patients in nursing homes;
Patients in emergency situations;
Homeless, nomads or refugees;
• Dislocation of the metatarsophalangeal joint (MTP joint)
• Complex regional pain syndrome
• Known allergy to the study device and or any of its components
• Fracture or deformities of accompanying bones (e.g. metatarsal bones)
• In the opinion of the investigator, patient has an emotional or neurological condition that would pre-empt their willingness to participate in the study, including mental illness, drug or alcohol abuse
• Patient is entered in another investigational drug or device study, or has been treated with an investigational product in the past 30 days
• Patient is suffering from restricted mobility that may impair post-operative healing
• Patient is known to be at risk for loss to follow-up or failure to return for scheduled study visits
• Patient is personally dependent on the investigator or the sponsor of the study
